back: Government policies, laws and regulations, and political stability, that affect how a business operates.

front: Areas of business the law controls
back: Employment practices, conditions of work, wages, marketing behaviour, competition, location and particular goods and services.
Laws and bodies that protect buyers from unsafe goods, false descriptions, misleading advertising and unfair terms.
Government action to prevent monopoly power, price-fixing and mergers that harm consumers.
Stability allows firms to plan and invest; instability brings uncertainty and discourages investment.

front: Legal requirements for starting an enterprise
back: Registration, licences, tax, labour law and consumer law.

front: Why small firms feel regulation more
back: Compliance cost is a larger share of revenue and they have fewer staff to handle it.

front: Ways to respond to legal change
back: Monitor proposals, adapt products and processes, train staff, lobby through trade associations, pass costs on in prices.
